01 / A brighter familiar world

The joy of Trickster.
Every action, felt.

A warm, painterly 2D isometric fan reimagining: recognizable adventurers, inviting towns and the pleasure of discovery, with deliberate posing and sharply readable action.

Trickster identityHades-inspired action clarityAI art productionIndependent review

AI visual exploration, not an approved Bunny model sheet, canonical map, or production asset. Costume consistency, town fidelity and camera calibration still need work.

The emotional target

Sunlit storybook adventure with a dangerous heartbeat.

Combat has intensity. Exploration has breathing room. Drilling and finding something wonderful have their own rhythm.

01

Recognize

Keep verified character landmarks, place identities, class fantasy and playful creature charm.

02

Feel

Use compression, decisive contact, recoil and clear recovery. Effects reinforce the action instead of covering it.

03

Return

Make town, companions and drilling as appealing as the fight. The world should feel worth staying in.

Package status: a detailed proposal and downstream handoff. No final art is accepted, no animation route is qualified, and no combat implementation is included.
02 / Preserve the soul

Familiar identities.
New expressive range.

This is a direct fan remake, as requested. Canonical reference comes before final redesign approval. Modernization should strengthen the identity people remember.

PreserveModernizeTest later
Animal-associated adventurers and class familiesCoherent model sheets, materials and action silhouettesAim/move separation; readable skill access

Power · Bunny / Buffalo

Compact load, planted contact, strong recoil. First playable art candidate: Bunny with one verified outfit and weapon interpretation.

Magic · Sheep / Dragon

Readable focus, release and recovery. Magic has a clear core and boundary rather than constant luminous fog.

Sense · Fox / Lion

Precise gesture and equipment handling. Aim, discovery and tool use need distinct silhouettes.

Charm · Cat / Raccoon

Welcoming idle, grounded protective gestures and confident presence. Charm should express agency in motion.

Family associations and historical interpretation are prior-knowledge synthesis awaiting reference verification. Proposed motion/gear are design studies, not authenticated original mechanics.

Canon-versus-modernization matrix: for every costume, skill, monster role and landmark, record what is verified, what deliberately changes and what remains unresolved. Proposed evade and elite behavior do not become canon by appearing in a concept.

03 / Sunlit ink and paint

Broad shapes.
Selective detail.

Confident contour hierarchy, warm light, cool occlusion and tactile materials. Save detail for places the eye should go.

Warm ground#F3DFBC
Coral#E98070
Sea teal#2AADB4
Deep ink#233B52
Sun gold#D5A64B
Skill cyan#81D5E8
Hostile accent#D94C49
Friendly accent#92B69A

Quiet floor, clear subjects

Sand and paths carry low-contrast texture. Faces, hands, weapon edges, threats and interactables have clearer structure. High-frequency ornament stays mostly at the scene edges.

Materials with restraint

Large matte cloth folds; decisive metal accents; sculptural coral and rock; broad water bands. Avoid photoreal noise and uniform shiny rendering.

Characters first

Verify ears, hair, costume blocks, hand policy and gear landmarks. Compare original proportions to a moderately taller action silhouette; approximately five heads is an optional study, not approved anatomy.

Painted light baseline

Broad upper-left light and separate contact shadows. Qualify one dynamic-light/normal-map sample before multiplying it across the library.

Calibration proposalMeaning
2:1 dimetric groundBasis (64,32), (-64,32); 128×64 reference diamond. Parallel projection, no perspective convergence.
1920×1080 referenceReview again at 1280×720. Actual readability matters more than source resolution.
512×512 actor sourceFixed foot anchor (256,420). No per-frame scale or camera changes.
320px body → 144px displayScale 0.45. Height means foot anchor to skull crown; excludes ears/headgear. Full canvas displays at 230.4px.
Eight view referencesScreen-space e, se, s, sw, w, nw, n, ne. Animation direction count remains a qualification decision.

All numbers are provisional targets for a later diagnostic scene. A painted concept board does not validate this camera or scale.

Read full visual bible
04 / Action with intention

Pose carries force.
Effects carry meaning.

An anticipation, a clear contact, a visible recovery. Responsive combat depends on phase timing, input and transitions as well as the drawings.

Load

Compress the silhouette and establish the direction. Body tells and enemy ground warnings agree.

Contact

Use decisive extension and a brief, localized accent. Show which target was hit without hiding the threat.

Recover

Make weight and commitment visible. Supply exit/interruption poses; cancellation rules remain prototype data.

Movement and aim

Eight facing views do not automatically solve strafing. Test backpedal/strafe motion or document a deliberate turn policy. Ground contact must agree with travel speed.

Enemy intelligence made visible

Notice, pursuit, reposition, windup, attack, recovery and interruption each need cues. Coordination should prevent a pile of indistinguishable overlapping warnings.

Drilling has a full arc

Plant → steady loop → resistance → reveal → retrieve → celebrate. Include abort and return-to-neutral. Keep the shaft and hands coherent at the ground contact.

Threat before decoration

Hostile boundaries use pattern, geometry and activation motion as well as color. Friendly effects, companion sparkles and loot yield visual priority.

The production bottleneck

A lovely keyframe does not prove a coherent animation.

Test controlled frame generation, layered 2D animation or AI-created rigged 3D sources rendered to sprites—only if the actual tools can deliver them. Compare the same small action/view set before selecting a route.

Illustrative six-action estimateFrames per facing
Idle / run / dodge6 + 8 + 6
Attack / hurt / drill10 + 3 + 8
Total at eight directions41 × 8 = 328 frames

Not a complete slice budget: skill, defeat, discovery/abort, companion and enemies add more. Frame count is not combat duration. At uncompressed RGBA8, 328 full 512² frames alone occupy 328 MiB before mipmaps/atlas padding; source resolution is not automatically the shipping export resolution.

Read animation and interaction briefs
05 / Places worth inhabiting

The fight is one rhythm.
The world has others.

Coral Beach / first field

Room to fight and discover

Verified coastal motifs, quiet traversable sand, a clear return path, a combat clearing and a calmer drilling pocket. Scenic palms and coral frame the action.

Ground, shoreline, cliffs, transitions, occluders, props and drill surfaces must form a reusable kit. The new layout is a proposal until compared with canonical references.

Megalopolis / social study

Make home recognizable

Verify architecture, landmarks, NPCs and palette before producing a town kit. Relaxed poses, discoverable shops and comfortable scale support the social mood.

The board's marketplace is a mood exploration, not authenticated Megalopolis. P1 covers a study and future kit plan, not a full playable city.

The map kit needs technical meaning

Ground anchorVisual boundsGround footprintTraversal guidanceOccluder policyAdjacency rules

Companions and finds

One verified companion with idle, follow, affection and discovery response. Ordinary and special finds have distinct feedback without constant spectacle.

A readable modern interface

Live text, restrained frames, clear skill status and contextual drill/interaction feedback. Icons must read at 32/48/64px and work beyond color alone.

Future coverage is planned, not commissioned: other regions, towns, heroes, bosses, equipment/cosmetics, portraits, quests, maps, collection systems, social UI and marketing art each have downstream brief coverage. No full-world asset multiplication before the slice passes.

07 / Parallelize families, protect consistency

More agents after
fewer unknowns.

The fastest reliable route is to resolve shared style and motion risks once, then give workers coherent families to produce. Splitting Bunny's frames across independent agents too early multiplies drift.

Reference and direction

Clear the pilot's canonical dependencies. Compare treatments using matching crops and scale. Other roster research can run independently.

Tiny route screen

Same hero: idle, run and attack in SE/NW plus E/W handedness evidence. Compare only available methods; select a viable route.

Broader pilot and shared freeze

Qualify direction coverage, dodge, hit, drilling, terrain, telegraph, impact and UI. Assemble actual-size scenes, then freeze camera, scale and file contracts.

Bounded family production

One enemy plus its full state family; one biome kit; one skill across phases; one UI component family. Each consumes the same approved source versions.

Independent acceptance and integration

Technical checks, art review, gameplay review, then coordinator acceptance. Rejected candidates never quietly enter exports.

Seven concurrent slotsResponsibility
1 · Coordinator / art directorBible, versions, dependency graph, scope and final acceptance
2 · Game design / implementation leadAction/AI/interaction semantics, gameplay review and technical continuity
3 · CHARHero, monster, companion and NPC source/reference families
4 · ENVModular environment kits, props and scene composition
5 · ANIMTool qualification, coherent actions, export and playback evidence
6 · VFX / UISeparate briefs executed sequentially as dependencies permit
7 · Independent REVIEWTechnical/art evidence and defect reports; no self-approval
At dual-review gates, pause/reassign a domain worker to review a family they did not create. Independent technical and art reviews need separate judgments, not an eighth concurrent slot. Keep unaffected work moving; do not fill slots with premature content.
Read DAG, role prompts and retry policy
08 / Review is a production stage

Evidence before
acceptance.

A producer self-checks. Independent reviewers inspect the entire batch. The coordinator accepts only after technical, art and gameplay gates agree.

Gate A · Reference and visual direction

Verified canon dependencies, comparable direction boards, actual-size silhouettes and a single coherent direction. Current package: not passed.

Gate B · Tool and import qualification

Actual source artifacts, registered animation playback, direction/handedness evidence, terrain adjacency, an impact, warning and drilling/discovery sample. A generated sheet is insufficient. Current package: not run.

Gate C · Shared composition freeze

Exploration, ordinary combat and deliberately dense combat in a real diagnostic scene. Check feet, range, occlusion, camera, HUD and warning priority together. Current package: not run.

Gate D · Family acceptance

Machine checks plus independent full-batch art/gameplay review, defect corrections and accepted hashes. Producer cannot accept their own work. Current package: no accepted assets.

Gate E · Assembled slice

Current-run playback and screenshots for discovery, interruption, ordinary/crowded combat, tall props and UI. Interactive feel review remains necessary. Current package: not run.

Technical review

Files, dimensions, alpha fringes, crop, pivots, frame order, direction map, import settings, atlas bleed and decoded memory. Source/provenance and transforms remain traceable.

Art review

Canon fidelity, anatomy and costume landmarks across all views, material consistency, camera, edge hierarchy and actual-size readability.

Gameplay review

Foot sliding, reach, tell/contact/recovery, transitions, overlap, tall props, drilling contact and companion priority. Stills cannot establish temporal quality.

Bounded rework

Initial candidate plus two targeted correction rounds. Then revise method/scope or reopen the contract. Keep reject evidence; never run unchanged prompts indefinitely.

An acceptance question

Where am I? What is about to hit? Where is safe? What did I hit? What can I discover?

If motion cannot answer those questions, the asset does not pass because its poster looks beautiful.

09 / Evidence and open decisions

Know what we know.
Label what we propose.

Verified

Official Godot 4.6 documentation source: sprite animation, TileMaps/TileSets, image import, 2D lighting, renderer differences and sorting APIs. Eleven source snapshots and hashes are archived.

Godot 4.6.3 passed the earlier headless engine smoke check. This does not validate graphics, art import or game behavior.

Not yet verified

Canonical costumes/maps/monsters, exact historical systems, Hades footage/timings and animation-tool production capability. Primary reference sites tried returned proxy 403.

No proprietary Hades pipeline or measured timings are claimed. Family/history descriptions are explicitly prior-knowledge synthesis.

# Copyable technical implementation kickoff

Use this prompt for a later implementation task. It is not authorization to implement during the current art-planning task.

---

You are the game-design and technical implementation lead for a **direct Trickster Online fan remake** with a modern painterly 2D isometric presentation and responsive, readable action inspired by Hades. The user selected a **PC combat slice first, online world later**. Preserve recognizable Trickster characters/locations, drilling/discovery, companion warmth and class identity. Do not replace the project with an unrelated original setting or expand immediately into MMO services.

Read the supplied art-direction package in this order: `README.md`, `visual-bible.md`, `research-and-decisions.md`, `game-design.md`, `production-playbook.md`, `asset-briefs.md`, the asset registry and any later qualification/review reports. The v0.1 package contains a concept board and plans, not production-ready assets. Current hero/place candidates are Bunny, Coral Beach and a Megalopolis social study; canonical detail verification is required. Use accepted assets only; visibly label temporary placeholders. Do not silently treat an attractive generated board as a runtime map, a model sheet or evidence of canon.

Inspect the actual repository, instructions, toolchain and existing work before changing anything. On 15 October 2026 the checkout was `/workspace/tricksterGodot`, empty/unborn, and Godot 4.6.3 was installed; recheck this rather than assuming it remains true. Use the existing checkout in its isolated task environment. Do not create a worktree unless explicitly requested. Preserve unrelated user work. Choose and document a practical Godot renderer after checking available rendering hardware; headless startup does not verify GPU rendering.

Start by auditing the available asset manifests, qualified animation route, reference provenance, camera calibration, source canvases, fixed foot origins, crop offsets, direction IDs, phase markers, filtering/mipmaps, alpha edges and texture-memory estimates. Missing canon evidence blocks final fidelity approval; missing animation capability blocks claims of production readiness. If the art gates have not passed, build a labeled diagnostic/blockout with placeholders and report those dependencies, rather than stopping independent technical preparation or pretending final art is integrated.

Build one compact representative field with:

- Responsive movement; keyboard/mouse and controller mappings; independent aim/facing where justified; explicit strafe/backpedal/turn presentation rather than sliding a forward-running sprite backward.
- Bunny primary action and one canon-reviewed skill adaptation, plus a tunable evade experiment. Maintain a canon-versus-modernization matrix for skill, weapon, evade and elite changes.
- Collision, ground-footprint navigation, feet-based sorting and a tested tall-prop occlusion policy. The provisional 2:1 dimetric ground basis is `(64,32),(-64,32)` with a 128×64 reference diamond. Normalize speed in the chosen simulation/world metric, not arbitrary projected screen length. Calibrate before fixing production exports.
- One close-range and one ranged enemy selected from verified Coral Beach references, and one deliberate elite adaptation. Implement readable notice, pursuit/reposition, windup, attack, recovery, interruption, defeat and return behavior as appropriate. Coordinate attack opportunities to avoid undifferentiated overlapping warnings.
- A drilling sequence with stable tool contact, progress/resistance, interrupt/abort, discovery/retrieve/celebrate and a return to neutral. Preserve its distinct pacing instead of reducing it to a generic loot button.
- A companion with follow, arrival, idle/emote and discovery response, safe offscreen recovery and low visual priority in combat. No pet combat economy required.
- Minimal HUD, skill status, interaction/drill feedback and pickup presentation with live text, scalable typography and controller focus.

Separate authoritative simulation and action data from animation presentation, VFX, input and UI. Emit semantic events (`anticipation`, `contact/active`, `recovery`, `exit`) for visuals; do not let sprite-frame callbacks own damage, invulnerability or network authority. Frame metadata can map visual phases, but simulation timing remains data-driven. Parameterize buffering, cancellations, dash invulnerability, aim assistance, telegraph durations, hit-stop and camera shake. These are prototype hypotheses, not measured Hades values or settled Trickster mechanics. Make reduced-effects/flash/shake settings available in the diagnostic build.

Use stable asset IDs, explicit actor states and local input-command boundaries that can later support networking. Do not implement accounts, servers, persistence, trading, guilds or multiplayer prediction until the offline slice proves its design. Future server authority will require a separate design; asset IDs alone do not make a game network-ready.

Deliver a diagnostic scene with actual-scale views, direction/facing markers, phase transitions, pivot overlays, collision/hit footprints, target-reach comparison, drilling contact and crowded effect overlap. Inspect exploration, normal combat, elite+ranged pressure, action behind tall props, interrupted drilling and companion recovery. Include screenshots/playback from actual rendering; selected stills cannot verify animation or combat feel.

Validation must exercise real state transitions, loading/import, contact timing, collision, interruption/recovery, sorting and input mapping. A zero-test run or an engine version command is insufficient. Run relevant automated state/data checks and headless import/startup, then interactive rendering/playtesting where available. Report limitations if interactive input or GPU capture is unavailable. Measure frame-time and decoded texture memory in the representative scene before claiming performance or selecting a final hardware target.

Return reproducible launch/build instructions, the playable slice or diagnostic project, test results with executed counts where applicable, rendering/playback evidence, performance observations, asset defects by ID and a concise list of design decisions still open. Do not expand to all eight playable characters, a full world, economy or MMO backend before slice acceptance. Do not disguise missing art, source access or tool capability as completed work.
